analysis.title: The bull market and the pendulum
key_insights: UBS CIO says global equities defied pessimists in 2026 despite war, energy price shocks, inflation, rising rates and growing government debt, helped by robust growth, rising productivity and rising corporate earnings.
Emerging markets and European equity indices outperformed Wall Street in 2026. Commodity prices and capital market yields rose across the board.
Equity indices sit near record highs while forward P/E valuations have fallen significantly. UBS argues rising profitability against falling valuations is a contrarian case for confidence in 2027.
Forward profit margins are at records: MSCI USA 16.9%, MSCI Canada 17.1%, MSCI Emerging Markets 13.9%, MSCI AC World ex USA 12.9%.
Forward P/E ratios: MSCI USA 18.5x, MSCI EMU 14.3x, MSCI Japan 14.1x, MSCI UK 12.0x, MSCI Emerging Markets 8.4x.
Base case for 2027: slightly higher global growth, US and Europe earnings up about 15%, AI infrastructure investment rising from USD 1tr to USD 1.4tr, and easing inflation.
Index targets: S&P 500 around 8,200, SMI around 15,500, Euro Stoxx 50 at 7,000.
Oil: global supply should exceed demand in 2027 for the first time, so Brent could fall to around USD 80 per barrel. US CPI is expected to fall to 2.6%, then 1.8% in 2028.
10-year yield targets in the base case: about 4.75% US, 2.95% Germany, 0.5% Switzerland.

UBS says AI must deliver. Many expected AI investments are already approved, ordered or under construction, and leading platform companies can self-finance a substantial share. Technology IPOs add transparency on returns.

Goldilocks scenario (20% probability): S&P 500 up to 9,000 and the US 10-year yield down to 4.00%. Two negative scenarios: an inflation and rate shock hurting both equities and bonds, and an AI downturn where quality bonds and gold act as counterweights.
The ten largest S&P 500 companies are about 40% of its value. UBS suggests equal-weighted indices, private markets, infrastructure and alternatives for diversification.

Fixed income rating moved back to Attractive after the rise in yields, particularly selected emerging markets and US high yield. Eurozone equities are rated attractive on 15% earnings growth at a lower valuation, with a defensive mix and large industrials and health care weights.

Swiss equities gained more than 7% from 16 September to 16 November while the S&P 500 lost about 2%. UBS weights Swiss, US and EM equities in line with strategic benchmarks, and likes industrials, health care, hyperscalers and semiconductor companies with strong balance sheets.
Copper could rise next year to around USD 15,500 per metric ton on demand from growth, the energy transition and electrification.

US government debt servicing costs have more than tripled in ten years, from about USD 433bn to about USD 1.36tr. UBS expects no general developed-market debt crisis in 2027 but more differentiation among borrowers.
UBS warns against extrapolating the past few years in a straight line and recommends active risk management and diversification rather than less risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Much of the expected AI investment is already approved, ordered or under construction, and leading platform companies can self-finance a substantial share. Faster monetization supports the Goldilocks case of S&P 500 at 9,000.
tension_points.bear_case: A technological revolution does not guarantee an attractive return on capital, and a possible AI downturn is one of two negative scenarios.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slow monetization of AI through earnings and productivity, which would produce the AI downturn scenario where quality bonds and gold act as counterweights.
